Problem: [RESOLVED] Toggling 'Show retrieval trace' after receiving an answer discarded the generated answer and the arrival context panel
Executive impact: Executive lost the answer they just read and had to trigger a second live (billed) Gemini call to see it again
Recommended change: Implemented: the RAG result is now persisted in a dedicated st.session_state key (RAG_RESULT_KEY) written once per explicit Investigate/Submit click, and rendered independently of the trace toggle. A 'Clear investigation' control was added for explicit resets. See app/views/rag_explorer.py and app/state.py.
Acceptance criterion: Retested live: toggling Show retrieval trace on and off after a successful query left the generated answer, evidence, and context panel visible throughout, with zero additional generator calls (verified both live and via mocked pytest tests in tests/test_app_cockpit.py).

Problem: [RESOLVED] Page text rendered at persistently low contrast/opacity on every load
Executive impact: First impression of an executive-facing tool looked broken or disabled, even though content was functionally correct
Recommended change: Root-caused (not an automation artifact): no .streamlit/config.toml, so Streamlit served its dark base theme for native text on top of the app's light-themed background. Implemented an explicit [theme] section in .streamlit/config.toml plus explicit Plotly chart colours.
Acceptance criterion: Retested live: body background rgb(246,248,251), heading colour rgb(27,42,74) -- full contrast confirmed via getComputedStyle, not just visual impression.

Problem: [RESOLVED] official_claims-type evidence rows were labelled 'Customer/creator-reported' source independence in RAG citations
Executive impact: An executive assessing evidence independence at a glance could have been misled about how corroborated a citation actually was
Recommended change: Root-caused: official_claims records were built with join_modality=None, so the claim-evidence-unit join never populated independence flags for them. Implemented explicit source_origin/independence_status fields via classify_evidence_provenance() (src/rag/schemas.py, src/rag/corpus_builder.py); Chroma index rebuilt via the existing idempotent scripts/build_chroma_index.py.
Acceptance criterion: Retested live and via regression tests for the 4 originally-cited claims (oc_0011/oc_0018/oc_0021/oc_0024) plus every source type: official_claims/official_reference/official_video/official_product_image now show 'Brand official / Self-reported'; customer_experience/creator_strategy are never defaulted to Independent.

Problem: [RESOLVED] Claim decision policy rows and roadmap phase cards were collapsed by default with no explicit 'click to expand' affordance
Executive impact: A first-time executive under time pressure might not have realised there was more content behind each collapsed row
Recommended change: Implemented: added 'Select a row to view its meaning, reviewer and permitted use' and 'Select a phase to view its owner, priority and completion criteria' captions above each expander group, and default-expanded the 'mixed' policy row and the current roadmap phase only.
Acceptance criterion: Retested live: both captions render, 'mixed' and 'Phase 0 - Academic prototype (current state)' render expanded by default, all other rows/phases remain collapsed.

Problem: [RESOLVED] Terms 'weight-sensitive' and 'presentation restriction' appeared in the claim detail panel before being explained anywhere else in the app
Executive impact: A first-time executive reading a claim detail card may not have understood these two fields without first visiting Methodology & Limitations
Recommended change: Implemented: added help= tooltips on the Fusion label, Weight-sensitive, Presentation restriction and Independent evidence metric cards on Claim Diagnostic, plus a new 'Key terms used in this cockpit' glossary section on Methodology & Limitations.
Acceptance criterion: Retested live: hovering the (?) icon on each of the four metrics shows the required one-sentence explanation; the Methodology glossary lists all 8 required terms.

Problem: A dedicated smaller-laptop responsive viewport pass and a systematic keyboard-only navigation accessibility pass have still not been completed
Executive impact: Responsive and keyboard-accessibility readiness for smaller screens and non-mouse users remains unverified
Recommended change: Schedule a follow-up, narrowly-scoped audit session covering only: (a) app behaviour at a smaller laptop viewport width, and (b) full keyboard-only navigation through all 6 pages and their interactive controls
Acceptance criterion: A follow-up audit report confirms or denies responsive/keyboard readiness with the same PASS/FAIL rigour as this report
